[
  {"task_id":"ctx-k7-1","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,9],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Zero pixels follow zero-based coordinates modulo 3: column residue 1 becomes 4, 6, or 3 for row residues 0, 1, or 2; column residue 2 becomes 5 only at row residue 0. Other pixels stay unchanged, as demonstrated throughout the first and second pairs."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k4-3","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,0,9,0,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Zero-based row and column parity determine recolouring: zeros at even/odd become 3, odd/even become 4, and odd/odd become 2. Colour 2 at even/even becomes 7, including positions (0,0) and (2,2) in the first demonstration."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k5-0","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,0,0,9,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Interior colours 1, 2, and 3 become 4, 5, and 9; border colour 3 becomes 0. In the first demonstration, interior (3,2) changes 1 to 4 while border (0,3) changes 3 to 0; border colours 1 and 2 remain unchanged."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k3-1","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,9,0,0,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Keys combine own colour with both nonzero row and column sets. In demonstration four, zeros with column set {2} become 4 in a row containing {1,2,3}, and 5 in rows containing {1,2}. Demonstration nine also maps colour 3 with row set {2,3} and column set {1,3} to 7."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k1-0","params":{"keysel":[0,9,0,0,0,0,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Nonzero row sets control recolouring: set {1,2,3} maps 0 to 7 and 2 to 6; set {2,3} maps 0 to 4; set {1,2} maps 1 to 8. The first, fifth, and second demonstrations respectively exhibit these mappings."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k3-0","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,9,0,0,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Both nonzero row and column sets are needed. In the first demonstration, column two has set {2,3}: its 3 becomes 5 and its 0 becomes 6 in rows with set {1,3}. In demonstration ten, colour 3 becomes 2 for row set {1,2,3} and column set {1,3}, while colour 2 becomes 4 when those sets are reversed."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k5-3","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,0,0,9,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Border zeros become 4 and border threes become 9; interior zeros become 5 and interior twos become 0. In the first demonstration, (0,0) changes 0 to 4, (1,1) changes 0 to 5, (1,2) changes 2 to 0, and (4,2) changes 3 to 9."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k1-3","params":{"keysel":[0,9,0,0,0,0,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Zeros are filled according to the nonzero row set: {1} gives 1, {3} gives 3, {1,3} gives 2, and {2,3} gives 1. The first demonstration shows the latter three mappings; the second shows singleton {1}. Rows containing {2}, {1,2}, or {1,2,3} remain unchanged."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k5-2","params":{"keysel":[0,0,0,0,0,9,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Zeros become 2 on the border and 3 inside; border ones become 0 and border twos become 4. Interior nonzero colours remain unchanged. Demonstration two shows border 1 to 0, interior 1 unchanged, and bottom-border 2 to 4."},
  {"task_id":"ctx-k0-0","params":{"keysel":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0],"bg":[9,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]},"rationale":"Full 3x3 patterns distinguish the sparse changes, including boundary padding. Demonstrations one and eight change an all-zero top-left neighbourhood centre to 2. Demonstration seven changes the left-edge zero with neighbourhood rows [-1,0,3], [-1,0,2], [-1,0,0] to 2, and its bottom-row zero surrounded by zeros and bottom padding to 8."}
]
